sections.label: Bootstrap Theme Colors
sections.guidance: Bootstrap's theme slots, remapped onto the brand palette. Setting these drives every `.text-*`, `.bg-*`, `.border-*`, `.btn-*` and `.alert-*`, so component styles should consume these rather than the brand tokens above.  These are only partly semantic. Primary, success, info and warning describe a role. Secondary, light and dark describe an appearance, so they say nothing about when to use them — a genuinely semantic name would read like "subtle text on a dark surface". Treat the appearance-named slots as Bootstrap's vocabulary rather than as this system's roles, and prefer a purpose-named token where one exists.

tokens.name: primary
tokens.note: Maroon. Reserved for calls to action.

sections.label: Semantic Surfaces and Text
sections.guidance: Low-contrast surfaces and de-emphasised text. These override Bootstrap's own roles, so the matching utilities work unchanged: `.bg-body-tertiary`, `.bg-body-secondary` and `.text-body-secondary`.

tokens.name: body-tertiary-bg
tokens.note: Subtlest page surface. Use for inset panels and code blocks.

tokens.name: body-secondary-bg
tokens.note: Slightly recessed surface, one step stronger than tertiary.

tokens.name: body-secondary-color
tokens.note: De-emphasised body text. Opaque, unlike Bootstrap's translucent default.

sections.label: Interactive and Inline Text Colors
sections.guidance: Links use the Lake family, not Primary. Maroon is reserved for calls to action so that a page's primary action stays visually unique.

sections.label: Active State Colors
sections.guidance: Active states use the Lake family for consistent interaction feedback.

sections.label: Focus Ring
sections.guidance: Keyboard focus is a solid outline drawn by `base/_global.scss`, not Bootstrap's translucent glow: the glow measured about 2:1 on white, below the 3:1 a focus indicator needs, and forced-colors mode removes box-shadows outright. Setting `$focus-ring-color` also feeds every Bootstrap component focus token, so this section is the single place focus colour is decided.

tokens.name: focus-ring-color
tokens.note: Focus outline on light surfaces. The link colour, so focus and links read as one family. At least 4.5:1 on white and on both body surfaces.

tokens.name: ucl-focus-ring-color-on-dark
tokens.note: Focus outline on dark surfaces — `.global-navbar`, `.navbar-dark` and `.footer` — where the link colour falls to about 2:1. The lighter shade of the same family, at least 4.3:1 on each.

tokens.name: font-family-sans-serif
tokens.value: "UChicago Sans Serif", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
tokens.note: The brand typeface, declared with its real weights in `base/_fonts.scss` and compiled into `main.css`, so no font stylesheet needs loading.

sections.label: Breadcrumb Overrides
sections.guidance: Level 3 component tokens. They live here because Bootstrap reads them while building its component styles, which happens after this file is imported.

sections.label: Accordion Overrides
sections.guidance: Level 3 component tokens. See the note on Breadcrumb Overrides above.

classes.note: Secondary column surface, marked by a maroon left edge. Use for supporting content beside the main column, not for content the page depends on. Typically used inside `.col-lg-4`.
Disclosure control inside a breadcrumb, for a trail segment that expands into sibling pages. Inherits the trail's size and weight so it does not read as a button.
Wrapper for the menu opened by `.breadcrumb-section-toggle`. Tightens Bootstrap's dropdown so it reads as part of the trail rather than a menu.
Bootstrap's button, restyled system-wide to a pill radius. Every button variant inherits this, so there is no square-cornered button in the system.

The large button, carrying semibold weight. A button at this size is a page's main call to action, and the heavier weight is what makes it read as one at a glance. The default and small sizes keep the body weight.
The standard action. Use for every button on a view except the one primary action, which is `.btn-primary`. Reads as an outlined secondary button.
Outlined button for use on a dark or image background, where the standard variants would have too little contrast.
Destructive action, outlined with a heavier border so it reads as needing deliberate intent. Reserve for actions that lose data.

A link inside an alert takes the alert's own link colour, as `.alert-link` does, without needing the class. The default link colour falls below 4.5:1 on most alert backgrounds; the alert's own is at least 5.4:1 on every variant. Colour only: add `.alert-link` for its bold weight as well.
Top bar holding the site logo, shortcut links and the mobile nav toggle. Sits above the global navbar and is separated from it by a bottom border.
Multi-column layout for a global-navbar dropdown, grouping links under headings. Only valid inside `.global-navbar`. Named in Bootstrap's `.dropdown-*` namespace but defined here, not by Bootstrap.
Heading for one group of links inside `.dropdown-layout`. Only valid inside `.global-navbar`. Named in Bootstrap's `.dropdown-*` namespace but defined here, not by Bootstrap.
Shortcut links shown inside the collapsed mobile menu, where the logo-bar shortcuts are hidden. Only valid inside `.global-navbar`.
Search region of the global navbar. Only valid inside `.global-navbar`.
Input wrapper inside `.global-navbar-search`, positioned so the submit button can overlay the field. Only valid inside `.global-navbar`.
Submit control overlaid on the right of `.global-navbar-search-field`. Only valid inside `.global-navbar`.
Site footer. Bootstrap has no footer component, so this is ours: a dark surface with white links and unstyled lists.
Column heading inside `.footer`. Only meaningful within `.footer`.
Centred block inside `.footer`, used for the logo and closing text. Legacy name kept for compatibility with existing footer markup.
Bootstrap's accordion.
Two-column accordion. Wrap the items in a Bootstrap `.row` with two columns; they stack below md. Each item keeps its own border and radius, since they are no longer a single vertical stack.

Bordered container for grouping related content. Equivalent to `.card.rounded-3.p-3`, as a single class. Use for a group that needs a visible boundary; use spacing alone when the grouping is already obvious.
Modifier for `.panel` that draws the border in maroon, marking the one group on a page that matters most. Do not use more than once per view.

sections.label: Primary Brand Colors
sections.guidance: The core UChicago palette. Brand tokens are the raw material of the system: prefer the semantic tokens further down when styling components, and reach for these only when defining a new semantic role.  Values follow the [UChicago Brand Guidelines](https://creative.uchicago.edu/brand-resources/), except Greystone: tinted to cooler greys for colour balance, with shades added to give a full neutral range for text, backgrounds and borders.

sections.label: Secondary Brand Colors - Lake Family
sections.guidance: The default family for active states, links and informational UI.
